nodes.description: In neuronal cells, PVNH-associated NEDD4L mutants raise phosphorylated S6 (mTORC1 activity) and phosphorylated AKT (Thr308 and Ser473), and disturb the cross-talk between AKT and Smad2/3 in activin/TGF-beta signalling. A patient lymphoblastoid cell line did not show increased AKT-mTOR activity, so the magnitude of the effect at endogenous expression is uncertain. Dab1 (Reelin pathway) disruption is not recorded here because, in the same study, it was caused by excess wild-type NEDD4L rather than by the patient mutants.

nodes.description: HECT-domain variants leave the ligase catalytically active, apparently enhancing its activity, while making the mutant protein sensitive to proteasomal degradation, so less NEDD4L protein carries more activity per molecule. A WW-domain variant is instead proposed to impair substrate recognition (loss of function); the direction of the net effect is recorded as a controversy in discussions.

nodes.description: In utero electroporation of PVNH mutants into the embryonic mouse cortex arrests neurons in the ventricular/subventricular and intermediate zones with depletion of the cortical plate, alters progenitor proliferation, and disrupts terminal translocation. The arrested neurons still acquire upper-layer identity, so the defect is in positioning rather than fate.

nodes.description: Heterozygous germline missense variants in NEDD4L. Nearly all reported variants map to the C-terminal catalytic HECT domain (for example p.Glu873Lys, p.Glu893Lys, p.Arg897Gln, p.Gln900Arg); the recurrent p.Arg208Gln lies in a WW substrate-recognition domain.

nodes.description: Bilateral (occasionally unilateral) nodules of grey matter lining the lateral ventricles; the MONDO-defining feature, present in all patients in the early case series.

evidence.reference_title: A novel missense mutation in the HECT domain of NEDD4L identified in a girl with periventricular nodular heterotopia, polymicrogyria and cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: All patients reported with NEDD4L HECT domain mutations showed periventricular nodular heterotopia, and most had seizures, cortex anomalies, cleft palate and syndactyly.

nodes.description: Variant transmitted from a father with about 10% somatic mosaicism to a daughter with PVNH, cleft palate and toe syndactyly, and to a fetus with hypokinesia and flexion contractures.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a girl with a novel heterozygous NEDD4L missense variant, p.Tyr679His, and characteristic clinical findings, including bilateral periventricular nodular heterotopia, cleft palate and mild toe syndactyly.
